scriptSegments.narration: Fifty-four percent of you blamed Guest Wi-Fi, while thirty-one percent nailed the real killer: the Smart Lobby Printer.

Tagged Tier-Four Public and ignored, that printer had scan-to-email enabled using an over-privileged Active Directory service account. Attackers dumped its cleartext LDAP password in ninety seconds and walked straight inside.

Static labels fail without Attack-Path Classification. Because of Transitive Trust, any Tier-Four device holding credentials or flat network routes into Tier-One inherits Crown Jewel risk. You never classify an asset only by the data sitting on it—you classify every identity and subnet it can touch.
Attackers proved this by stealing ten gigabytes of casino VIP data through a lobby fish-tank thermometer, echoing Target's HVAC pivot.
Regulators audit NovaPay tomorrow morning. How do we eliminate shadow pivots permanently: Quarterly Spreadsheets, Continuous Auto-Discovery, or IoT Bans? Comment below.
